name: Manjyly-Ata Valley
full: Manjyly-Ata Valley (the sacred springs of Manjyly-Ata)
near: Tong village — ~5 km to the northwest (Aigine); Bokonbaevo — ~10 min by car to the west (Backpack Adventures, 2026); Kaji-Say — ~15 min to the east. The complex is ~1 km from the lakeshore, south of the Bishkek — Karakol highway.
elev: ~1650 m (Nomad's Land) — hills 1 km from the shore, slightly above the lake level (1607 m).
short: A valley of sacred springs on the south shore of Issyk-Kul: 7–17 mineral springs among clay hills and old willows, a saint's mazar, a caretaker-shyrakchy and pilgrims from all over Kyrgyzstan; a place from the Manas epic, reachable from the highway in 10 minutes from Bokonbaevo.
desc: Manjyly-Ata is a maze of dry clay valleys (a “geological anomaly,” per Nomad's Land) between the highway and the Terskey foothills, 5 km southeast of Tong village. According to a study by the Aigine center, there are seven main springs here, each with a name and a “specialization”: Manjyly-Ata (the main one, ringed by black willows), Maytyk-Dubana, Ilim, Bala, Bugu-Ene, Aziz, Uy-Bulyolyuk — for ailments from infertility to liver and eye diseases; guidebooks count 12 main and 5 additional springs (17 in all). On the hill is the mazar of an Islamic preacher, where the round of the springs begins; the tradition blends Tengrism and Islam, and the place is mentioned in the Manas epic and became famous by the end of the 17th century. The caretaker (as of 2026, Zhakypov Kadyrbek, a healer from Jeti-Oguz) guides pilgrims and explains the properties of the water. A full round of the springs takes about 2 hours on foot along dry, shadeless paths. Religious leaders complain that the water in the springs is diminishing (drought, groundwater pumping) and that “entertainment” tourism robs the place of its power — kasiet (Religion News, 2024). There are no entrance tickets; a donation to the caretaker is customary (the amount is not set).
guide: This is not a park but a living shrine: come as a guest, not as a tourist — cover your shoulders and knees, keep your voice low, don't step into the water with shoes on, and ask the caretaker before drinking from a spring. Walking the seven to twelve springs takes a couple of hours over dry, shadeless hills, so morning or evening and a liter of water are essential. Each spring has its own “specialty” — the most famous is the one childless couples travel to. Climb up to the mazar on the hill: from there you can see the lake and the same “Martian” clay as in the neighboring canyons. No fee is charged, but leaving a donation for the caretaker is the right thing to do. Combine it with Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon (20 km) and the Shatyly panorama — all of it fits into one day based in Bokonbaevo.
see: The main Manjyly-Ata spring ringed by black willows; the springs Maytyk-Dubana, Ilim, Bala, Bugu-Ene, Aziz (you can hear water inside a willow trunk), Uy-Bulyolyuk; the mazar on the hill with a view of the lake; the “eight sacred willows”; healing mud nearby; a landscape of dry clay hills that merges into the Mars canyons (0.5 km).
skip: You're uncomfortable at active religious sites with rules of conduct. You expect waterfalls and “bathing pools” — the springs are small, the water is for drinking and ablution, not for swimming. Heat above 30 °C: there's no shade at all.
diff: Easy: a walk over gentle dry hills and hollows, ~2 h for the full round (Backpack Adventures, 2026); no elevation gain; no shade and no water (apart from the springs).
when: Year-round (Backpack Adventures): there is almost no snow in winter, but it's cold; summer is hot and shadeless — April–June and September–October are more comfortable. On Fridays and religious holidays there are more pilgrims.
hours: Google Maps (03.10.2026): open 24 hours. In practice, daylight hours; the caretaker lives at the complex, and it's best to arrange a tour through CBT Bokonbaevo.
daytime: Early morning or 2 hours before sunset — cool, soft light on the clay hills; midday in summer is hot.
how: On the southern Balykchy — Karakol highway (A363) between Bokonbaevo and Kaji-Say: a large sign by the road (Backpack Adventures), turn south to the springs. From Bokonbaevo — 10 min by taxi (via CBT Bokonbaevo) or a marshrutka (minibus) toward Kaji-Say to the sign; from Karakol — a marshrutka toward Bokonbaevo ~2 h, ~100 som (TripAdvisor 2018; more expensive now), get off at the sign. From Bishkek — a marshrutka to Bokonbaevo 550–650 som (2025).
needcar: Yes for convenience: it's 8–10 km from Bokonbaevo; you can take a marshrutka along the highway and walk ~1 km from the road. Within the valley — on foot only.
self: Yes: entry is free, the paths between the springs are readable, but without a guide it's easy to miss some of the springs (TripAdvisor); a dress code and respect for pilgrims are mandatory.
roadtype: Paved road along the A363 highway; the turn-off is a dirt/clay road to the springs (passable by an ordinary car in dry weather); then footpaths over clay (slippery after rain).
traveltime: Bokonbaevo — Manjyly-Ata 10 min; Kaji-Say — 15 min; Karakol — ~2 h; Bishkek — ~5 h. A round of the springs — ~2 h (Backpack Adventures, 2026), a short visit — 1 h.
stay: On site — the Manjyly-Ata yurt camp (6 yurts without beds; prices on request, 2020 data — jartour.ru; operation in 2025–2026 not confirmed). Base: Bokonbaevo — guesthouses Nurgul, Guljan, Gulmira, Ayim (Backpack Adventures 2026), Baiel, Akbermet, Amirhan, Ecoresort Kaiyrma (Journal of Nomads 2025); CBT and Bel-Tam yurt camps on the shore. Prices not published.
net: Along the highway between Bokonbaevo and Kaji-Say there is operator coverage (MegaCom 4G in Bokonbaevo since 2019 — Kaktus.media); in the hollows of the valley the signal may drop out — no direct tests were found.
entry: There is no entrance fee (no source from 2017–2026 mentions one); a donation to the caretaker/the mazar is customary — the amount is up to you. The caretaker's tour is by arrangement.
transfer: Taxi from Bokonbaevo — not published; marshrutka Karakol — Bokonbaevo ~100 som (TripAdvisor, 2018); Bishkek — Bokonbaevo 550–650 som (Journal of Nomads, 2025).
bring: Modest clothing (shoulders, knees covered; a headscarf is desirable for women), 1–1.5 L of water, a hat and sun protection, shoes with firm soles (clay, thorns), small cash for a donation, an empty bottle — pilgrims collect water from the springs.
warn: An active pilgrimage site: don't make noise, don't photograph people at prayer without permission, don't wash your feet/shoes in the springs, don't leave trash; the “healing” quality of the water is a local belief, not a medical fact, and drinking safety is not guaranteed (boil it). In summer the heat is shadeless; after rain the clay is slippery. The springs are drying up (2024) — in a dry year some may be empty.
food: There is no food on site. In Bokonbaevo — the Argymak cafe (Mambetov St. 16), home-cooked lunches at guesthouses, smoked fish along the highway; in the yurt camps — beshbarmak and kumys. Specific establishments have not been checked.
reviews: Google Maps “Manjyly-Ata”: 4.7/5, 55 ratings (03.10.2026). TripAdvisor “Manjyly-Ata Valley”: 4.0/5, 2 reviews (2015–2018). Pros: authenticity, quiet, scenery, free; cons: it's hard to find all the springs without a guide, infrequent transport, no shade.
p.sum: A shrine right by the southern highway between Bokonbaevo and Kaji-Say: a large sign on the road, then a turn south ~1 km along a dirt road to the mazar and the springs (Google marker 42.1478, 77.0858). Base: Bokonbaevo (10 minutes by taxi); without a car — any marshrutka along the south shore, asking to be dropped at the sign. Entry is free, a donation to the caretaker is customary; the full round of the springs takes ~2 h over dry, shadeless hills, so morning/evening, water and modest clothing are essential.

p.iti.0.title: A morning on the south shore
p.iti.0.plan: 5:00 sunrise at Shatyly → 8:00 breakfast in Bokonbaevo → 9:00–11:00 round of the Manjyly-Ata springs with the caretaker → Mars canyons → lunch in Kaji-Say → evening — Skazka (Fairy Tale) Canyon.
p.iti.1.title: 2 days from Bishkek
p.iti.1.plan: Day 1: Bishkek → Bokonbaevo (5–6 h), in the evening Manjyly-Ata and the eagle-hunter show, night in a yurt. Day 2: Shatyly at sunrise → Skazka → Tosor/Tamga beach → Bishkek or Karakol.
p.iti.2.title: Route combination
p.iti.2.plan: Bokonbaevo → Manjyly-Ata → Mars canyons → Shatyly → Kaji-Say → Skazka → Barskoon.
p.season: Year-round. April–June and September–October are comfortable; July–August is shadeless heat, go only in the morning/evening; winter has almost no snow, cold. Fridays and religious holidays — more pilgrims.
p.budget.economy: Marshrutka Bishkek — Bokonbaevo 550–650 (or Karakol ~150); 1 km on foot from the highway; donation 50–200 at your discretion; guesthouse 350–1,500. ≈ 1,500–2,500 som/person.
p.budget.comfort: Shared taxi 800–1,000 or a car 3,500–4,000; taxi from Bokonbaevo with a wait; yurt camp/eco-resort; excursion through CBT. ≈ 4,000–7,000 som/person.
p.permits: Not needed; no entrance fee. A donation to the caretaker/the mazar is customary.
p.access: Easy terrain — children and older people can manage, but the heat and lack of shade in summer; a stroller only near the turn-off (clay paths); it's best not to bring dogs to the shrine.
